categories.main_business_segments: S&P Global operates six reportable segments: S&P Global Market Intelligence (multi-asset-class data and analytics), S&P Global Ratings (credit ratings and research), S&P Global Commodity Insights (commodity and energy market information), S&P Global Mobility (automotive solutions), S&P Dow Jones Indices (index benchmarks), and S&P Global Engineering Solutions (engineering standards and technical knowledge). The company serves capital, commodity, automotive, and engineering markets globally.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company leverages advanced data analytics, proprietary methodologies, machine learning, and cloud-based infrastructure (particularly AWS) to develop its products and services. Core technologies include knowledge discovery systems, cognitive search capabilities, software-based engineering decision engines, benchmark development and administration, price assessment methodologies, and workflow automation solutions. The company is transitioning to cloud-based infrastructure and investing in artificial intelligence applications across its offerings.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Primary customers include asset managers, investment banks, commercial banks, insurance companies, exchanges, trading firms, corporate issuers, governments, municipalities, commodity producers and traders, automotive manufacturers and suppliers, dealerships, engineers, builders, and architects. End markets span global capital markets, commodity and energy markets, automotive industry, and engineering sectors. The company serves approximately 39,950 employees across 21,750 in Asia, 11,750 in U.S. and Canada, 5,700 in Europe/Middle East/Africa, and 750 in Latin America.
categories.geographic_coverage: S&P Global operates globally with significant presence in the United States (60% of revenue), Europe (23% of revenue), Asia (11% of revenue), and Rest of World (6% of revenue). The company has offices in over 25 countries for its Ratings business and operates across major geographic regions including North America, Europe, Asia-Pacific, and Latin America. Headquarters are located in New York City.
categories.supply_chain_position: S&P Global operates primarily in the midstream and downstream portions of information supply chains, providing data, analytics, ratings, benchmarks, and workflow solutions to financial institutions, corporations, and other market participants. The company relies on upstream data suppliers and third-party service providers (including AWS for cloud infrastructure) while distributing its products through both proprietary and third-party channels to end customers.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategic priorities include: realizing merger integration commitments and synergies from the IHS Markit acquisition; enhancing customer experience through seamless integration of capabilities; investing in growth areas including ESG, sustainability data, and artificial intelligence; transitioning to cloud-based infrastructure; improving data governance and enterprise data management; advancing diversity, equity and inclusion; and driving innovation in product development. The company emphasizes 'Powering the Markets of the Future' through foundational capability enhancement, core business evolution, and growth via adjacencies.
categories.revenue_model: S&P Global generates revenue through multiple streams: subscription revenue (55% of total, from data distribution, software licenses, and platform access); non-subscription/transaction revenue (16%, from ratings issuances and bank loan ratings); non-transaction revenue (15%, from surveillance fees and research); asset-linked fees (8%, from ETFs and mutual funds based on assets under management); sales usage-based royalties (3%, from exchange-traded derivatives); and recurring variable revenue (3%, from usage-based contracts). Revenue is derived from both recurring subscriptions and transactional services.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: S&P Global competes with traditional content and analytics providers including Moody's Corporation, CME Group, MSCI Inc., FactSet Research Systems, Verisk Analytics, and Intercontinental Exchange. The company also faces competition from non-traditional providers including asset managers, investment banks, private equity firms, and technology-led companies that are developing competing capabilities. S&P Global maintains a leading market position through its established brands, global network, and comprehensive product portfolio across multiple markets.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: S&P Global is a large-cap company with 2022 revenue of $11.2 billion (35% increase from 2021), operating profit of $4.9 billion (17% increase), and net income of $3.2 billion. The company has approximately 322 million shares outstanding and a market capitalization of approximately $113.3 billion as of mid-2022. The company demonstrates consistent growth with 11% revenue growth in 2021 and 35% in 2022 (including IHS Markit merger impact), reflecting both organic growth and acquisition-driven expansion.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: S&P Global differentiates through: independent credit ratings and benchmarks with over 150 years of market infrastructure role; comprehensive multi-asset-class data and analytics integrated with workflow solutions; proprietary methodologies and quality research; global scale and geographic reach; brand reputation and credibility in financial markets; advanced technology platforms and cloud infrastructure; and integrated capabilities across ratings, data, indices, and analytics. The company emphasizes independence, integrity, and innovation in serving global markets with transparent benchmarks and decision-making tools.
